question: Explain the Net Present Value (NPV) method of evaluating investment proposals, with its merits and limitations.
sources: Capital budgeting: discounted cash flow techniques (net present value method)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: NPV is the present value of expected cash inflows minus the present value of cash outflows, discounted at the firm's cost of capital.

points.label: Decision rule
points.description: Accept a project if NPV is positive and reject it if negative; among mutually exclusive projects, prefer the one with the higher NPV.

points.label: Merits: time value and all cash flows
points.description: It considers the time value of money and all cash flows over the whole life of the project.

points.label: Merits: link to wealth
points.description: It is consistent with maximising shareholders' wealth, and NPVs of projects can be added together.

points.label: Limitations
points.description: It needs an estimate of the cost of capital and of future cash flows, and it may not rank well projects of very different size or life.
